description:
OBJECTIVE: Beth currently has ZERO skill references in beth.agent.md. When she works directly (simple tasks, quick fixes, or decides not to delegate), she operates without any domain knowledge from the skills directory. This task adds an explicit skill routing table so Beth knows which skills exist, which agents own them, and can reference them when working directly or instructing subagents.

IMPLEMENTATION:

2. Add a new "## Skill Routing" section AFTER the "## Your Team" section and BEFORE "## How You Operate"
3. Insert this exact content:

## Skill Routing

When working directly or instructing subagents, load the appropriate skill for the domain:

| Domain | Skill File | Primary Agent | Load When |
|--------|-----------|---------------|-----------|
| Requirements/PRD | `.github/skills/prd/SKILL.md` | product-manager | Defining features, writing specs |
| UI Components | `.github/skills/shadcn-ui/SKILL.md` | developer | Building UI with shadcn components |
| Framer Components | `.github/skills/framer-components/SKILL.md` | developer, ux-designer | Framer property controls, overrides |
| React Performance | `.github/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md` | developer | React/Next.js optimization |
| Security Analysis | `.github/skills/security-analysis/SKILL.md` | security-reviewer | Security audits, OWASP, threat models |
| Web Research | `.github/skills/web-search/SKILL.md` | researcher | Competitive analysis, market research |
| Design Audit | `.github/skills/web-design-guidelines/SKILL.md` | tester, ux-designer | UI review, accessibility audit |
| Azure Ops | `.github/skills/azure-operations/SKILL.md` | developer | Azure resource management |

**Rules:**
- When working directly on a task that falls in a skill domain, read the SKILL.md BEFORE starting work
- When spawning subagents, ALWAYS include "Load and follow: <skill-path>" for relevant skills in the prompt
- If a task spans multiple domains, load all relevant skills

## Task: <beads-id>: <title>

description:
OBJECTIVE: Beth's 6 outbound handoffs in her frontmatter use sparse, generic one-liner prompts like "Define WHAT to build - user stories, acceptance criteria, prioritization, roadmap, and success metrics". When a user manually clicks a handoff button in the UI (rather than Beth spawning a subagent programmatically), the receiving agent gets ONLY this generic sentence — no project context, no specific feature details. The user has to re-explain everything. This task makes handoff prompts richer and adds send: true where appropriate.

HOW TO VERIFY THE PROBLEM:
1. Open .github/agents/beth.agent.md frontmatter
2. Look at the handoffs: section — all 6 have send: false
3. Each prompt is a single generic sentence with no specificity

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Open .github/agents/beth.agent.md
2. Replace the handoffs: block in the YAML frontmatter with:

handoffs:
  - label: Product Strategy
    agent: product-manager
    prompt: "Define WHAT to build. Load `.github/skills/prd/SKILL.md`. Create user stories with acceptance criteria, RICE prioritization, and success metrics. Check `AGENTS.md` for tracking protocol."
    send: true
  - label: User Research
    agent: researcher
    prompt: "Conduct research to validate product assumptions. Load `.github/skills/web-search/SKILL.md` for web research capabilities. Synthesize findings into actionable insights. Check `AGENTS.md` for tracking protocol."
    send: true
  - label: UX Design
    agent: ux-designer
    prompt: "Specify HOW it works. Load `.github/skills/framer-components/SKILL.md` and `.github/skills/web-design-guidelines/SKILL.md`. Deliver component specs, interaction states, design tokens, and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility requirements. Check `AGENTS.md` for tracking protocol."
    send: true
  - label: Development
    agent: developer
    prompt: "Implement in React/TypeScript/Next.js. Load `.github/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md` and `.github/skills/shadcn-ui/SKILL.md`. Follow Server Components-first pattern. Check `AGENTS.md` for tracking protocol."

    send: true
  - label: Quality Assurance
    agent: tester
    prompt: "Test and verify quality. Load `.github/skills/web-design-guidelines/SKILL.md`. Cover functionality, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility, performance (Core Web Vitals), and edge cases. Check `AGENTS.md` for tracking protocol."
    send: true

KEY CHANGES:
- send: false → send: true (conversation context transfers)
- Each prompt now includes: which SKILL.md to load, specific deliverables, and AGENTS.md reference
- Kept prompts concise (1-2 sentences) but actionable
